newsitem.title: INDIA: India Petronet to undertake pipeline study.
newsitem.headline: India Petronet to undertake pipeline study.

text.p: Petronet India Limited, a holding company formed by four state-run oil firms to identify future product pipelines, will do a detailed evaluation of five product pipelines, Indian Oil Corp (IOC) said on Tuesday.
IOC said in a statement that the study would cover a total lenth of more than 1700 km.

Petronet India, set up on May 26 to construct and operate petroleum product pipelines through its joint ventures and subsidiaries, agreed to do the evaluation at its first board meeting on Monday, the statement said.
The pipleines identified for detailed evaluation are Vadinar-Kandla, Cochin-Karur, Bangalore-Mangalore, Chennai-Trichy-Madurai and Bina-Jhansi-Kanpur.

Indian Oil, Bharat Petroleum Corp and Hindustan Petroleum Corp will hold 16 percent equity each in the company. IBP Co Ltd will hold two percent equity and the remaining 50 percent will be held by financial institutions, private companies and the public.
IOC chairman M.A. Pathan was appointed chairman of Petronet which will have its headquarters in Bombay.
